MATHEMATICS — TERMLY EXAM #20 (TERM 2)
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: MATHEMATICS
TIME ALLOWED: 60 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 50
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. If a = 4, what is the value of 3a? (1 mark)
   A. 1
   B. 34
   C. 7
   D. 12

2. Simplify 6p − p. (1 mark)
   A. 6p
   B. 7p
   C. 6
   D. 5p

3. Simplify 3a + 2a. (1 mark)
   A. 5
   B. 5aa
   C. 6a
   D. 5a

4. A fence uses 3 pieces of wire, each 1 m 25 cm long. What is the total length of wire? (1 mark)
   A. 1 m 28 cm
   B. 4 m 75 cm
   C. 3 m 65 cm
   D. 3 m 75 cm

5. Change 12 m to centimetres. (1 mark)
   A. 12 cm
   B. 1,200 cm
   C. 12,000 cm
   D. 120 cm

6. What is 8 m − 3 m 40 cm? (1 mark)
   A. 4 m 70 cm
   B. 4 m 60 cm
   C. 4 m 50 cm
   D. 5 m 60 cm

7. A rectangle is made of 10 rows with 10 unit squares in each row. What is its area? (1 mark)
   A. 40 square units
   B. 20 square units
   C. 100 square units
   D. 110 square units

8. A rectangle is made of 5 rows with 8 unit squares in each row. What is its area? (1 mark)
   A. 13 square units
   B. 45 square units
   C. 26 square units
   D. 40 square units

9. A square is covered with 5 rows of 5 unit squares. What is its area? (1 mark)
   A. 30 square units
   B. 20 square units
   C. 25 square units
   D. 10 square units

10. Why should heavy boxes be stacked at the bottom? (1 mark)
   A. So that the boxes are hidden
   B. So that the stack is stable and does not fall
   C. So that the volume increases
   D. It makes no difference

11. A cuboid is 5 blocks long, 4 blocks wide and 4 blocks high. What is its volume? (1 mark)
   A. 13 blocks
   B. 20 blocks
   C. 85 blocks
   D. 80 blocks

12. A cuboid is 6 blocks long, 3 blocks wide and 2 blocks high. What is its volume? (1 mark)
   A. 36 blocks
   B. 18 blocks
   C. 42 blocks
   D. 11 blocks

13. What is 2 1/4 L + 1 1/2 L? (1 mark)
   A. 3 3/4 L
   B. 4 1/4 L
   C. 4 L
   D. 3 1/2 L

14. What is 6 1/4 L − 2 1/2 L? (1 mark)
   A. 3 3/4 L
   B. 3 1/2 L
   C. 4 1/4 L
   D. 4 L

15. A shopper buys 3/4 kg of tomatoes and 1/2 kg of onions. What is the total mass? (1 mark)
   A. 5/8 kg
   B. 1 kg
   C. 1 1/4 kg
   D. 1 1/2 kg

16. A dial scale pointer stops halfway between 3 and 4. What is the mass? (1 mark)
   A. 3 kg
   B. 3 1/2 kg
   C. 3 1/4 kg
   D. 4 kg

17. An electronic balance shows 2.5 kg. Which mass is this? (1 mark)
   A. 25 kg
   B. 2 1/2 kg
   C. 2 1/4 kg
   D. 2 3/4 kg

18. On an analogue clock the short hour hand has reached or passed the number 4 but not yet reached the next number, and the long minute hand points to the number 4. What time is shown? (1 mark)
   A. 4:20
   B. 4:40
   C. 5:20
   D. 4:04

19. How many days are in 3 weeks? (1 mark)
   A. 21 days
   B. 28 days
   C. 72 days
   D. 15 days

20. How long is a lesson that starts at 1:15 p.m. and ends at 4:50 p.m.? (1 mark)
   A. 3 h 45 min
   B. 3 h 20 min
   C. 4 h 35 min
   D. 3 h 35 min

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
21. Explain how you can compare the areas of two sheets of paper without using a ruler. (2 marks)

22. A trip leaves at 7:45 a.m. and takes 2 hours 30 minutes. At what time does it arrive? (3 marks)

23. A lesson starts at 8:15 a.m. and ends at 10:40 a.m. How long is the lesson? (3 marks)

24. Work out 6 1/4 kg − 2 3/4 kg. (3 marks)

25. The mass of a basket full of mangoes is 8 kg and the basket alone is 1 1/2 kg. Find the mass of the mangoes alone. (2 marks)

26. A learner says 3 weeks is 20 days. Explain her mistake and give the correct number of days. (3 marks)

27. Add 2 1/2 kg and 1 3/4 kg. Show your working. (3 marks)

28. Write these times using a.m. or p.m.: (a) waking up at half past six in the morning, (b) school ending at a quarter past three in the afternoon, (c) supper at half past seven at night. (3 marks)

29. A trader has 12 kg of beans and 8 kg of maize. He sells 5 kg of the beans. Find the total mass of the beans and maize he has left. (3 marks)

30. A jerrycan holds 5 L. Musa pours out 2 1/2 L. How much is left in the jerrycan? (2 marks)

31. A rectangle has an area of 48 square units and 6 rows. How many columns does it have? Explain how you found out. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
MATHEMATICS — TERMLY EXAM #20 (TERM 2) · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — 12
   Replace the letter by its value and work it out. The answer is 12.

2. D — 5p
   Only like terms can be joined. 6p − p = 5p.

3. D — 5a
   Only like terms can be joined. 3a + 2a = 5a.

4. D — 3 m 75 cm
   125 × 3 = 375 cm = 3 m 75 cm.

5. B — 1,200 cm
   1 m = 100 cm. 12 × 100 = 1200. So the answer is 1,200 cm.

6. B — 4 m 60 cm
   800 − 340 = 460 cm = 4 m 60 cm.

7. C — 100 square units
   Area = rows × columns = 10 × 10 = 100 square units.

8. D — 40 square units
   Area = rows × columns = 5 × 8 = 40 square units.

9. C — 25 square units
   Area = 5 × 5 = 25 square units.

10. B — So that the stack is stable and does not fall
   A stack with heavy boxes at the bottom is more stable and safer.

11. D — 80 blocks
   One layer has 5 × 4 = 20 blocks. There are 4 layers, so the volume is 20 × 4 = 80 blocks.

12. A — 36 blocks
   One layer has 6 × 3 = 18 blocks. There are 2 layers, so the volume is 18 × 2 = 36 blocks.

13. A — 3 3/4 L
   Work with the whole litres first and then the parts. 2 1/4 L + 1 1/2 L = 3 3/4 L.

14. A — 3 3/4 L
   Work with the whole litres first and then the parts. 6 1/4 L − 2 1/2 L = 3 3/4 L.

15. C — 1 1/4 kg
   3/4 + 2/4 = 5/4 = 1 1/4 kg.

16. B — 3 1/2 kg
   Halfway between 3 kg and 4 kg is 3 1/2 kg.

17. B — 2 1/2 kg
   0.5 is half, so 2.5 kg is 2 1/2 kg.

18. A — 4:20
   Each number on the clock face is worth 5 minutes. The minute hand at 4 shows 4 × 5 = 20 minutes, so the time is 4:20.

19. A — 21 days
   1 week = 7 days, so 3 × 7 = 21 days.

20. D — 3 h 35 min
   Count on from 1:15 p.m. to 4:50 p.m.. The total is 3 h 35 min.

SECTION B
----
21. (2 marks)
   Answer: Put one sheet on top of the other with their corners lined up. The sheet that sticks out has the bigger area.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for placing one on the other and 1 mark for saying the one that sticks out is bigger.

22. (3 marks)
   Answer: 10:15 a.m.
   Working / marking points: 7:45 + 2 h = 9:45 (1 mark); 9:45 + 30 min = 10:15 (1 mark); a.m. stated (1 mark).

23. (3 marks)
   Answer: 2 hours 25 minutes
   Working / marking points: 8:15 to 10:15 is 2 hours (1 mark); 10:15 to 10:40 is 25 minutes (1 mark); total 2 h 25 min (1 mark).

24. (3 marks)
   Answer: 3 1/2 kg
   Working / marking points: Change 6 1/4 to 5 5/4 (1 mark); wholes 5 − 2 = 3 and quarters 5/4 − 3/4 = 1/2 (1 mark); answer 3 1/2 kg (1 mark).

25. (2 marks)
   Answer: 6 1/2 kg
   Working / marking points: 8 − 1 1/2 = 6 1/2. 1 mark for the subtraction and 1 mark for the unit.

26. (3 marks)
   Answer: 1 week has 7 days, so 3 weeks is 3 × 7 = 21 days.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for 7 days in a week, 1 mark for multiplying by 3, 1 mark for 21 days.

27. (3 marks)
   Answer: 4 1/4 kg
   Working / marking points: Wholes 2 + 1 = 3 (1 mark); parts 2/4 + 3/4 = 5/4 = 1 1/4 (1 mark); total 4 1/4 kg (1 mark).

28. (3 marks)
   Answer: (a) 6:30 a.m. (b) 3:15 p.m. (c) 7:30 p.m.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct time with a.m. or p.m.

29. (3 marks)
   Answer: 15 kg
   Working / marking points: 12 − 5 = 7 kg of beans (1 mark); 7 + 8 (1 mark); 15 kg (1 mark).

30. (2 marks)
   Answer: 2 1/2 L
   Working / marking points: 5 − 2 1/2 = 2 1/2. 1 mark for the subtraction and 1 mark for the unit.

31. (3 marks)
   Answer: 8 columns. Area = rows × columns, so columns = 48 ÷ 6 = 8.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the relationship, 1 mark for the division, 1 mark for 8.
